objective: Narrate an ordinary day — waking, eating, working, coming home. Everyday habitual actions are exactly what the b- present is for, so this unit is where that pattern starts paying off.

grammar.point: The b- present is the everyday tense
grammar.body: بَصْحى، بَاكُل، بَشْتْغِل — the بـ on the front marks what you habitually do. It is the workhorse tense of ordinary talk, and a daily routine is the cleanest place to drill it.

drills.title: Practice
drills.instructions: Answer out loud, in Arabic, in full sentences.

items.cue: 1) Prepare to speak about your weekly routine in Givat Haviva,
2) Speak about your routine as a student in your country and a Saturday routine.
3) Speak about your preferred daily routine.

produce: Tell your whole day in order, out loud, in the b- present. Then tell it again about someone else in your family (he/she forms).
